newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador angered by U.S. charges of corruption.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador angered by U.S. charges of corruption.

text.p: Ecuador's President Abdala Bucaram hit back angrily at the United States on Thursday after accusations by the U.S. ambassador that the country was increasingly riddled by corruption.
"They should leave us alone. Let them leave us in peace and not interfere with our sovereignty," Bucaram told local television.
A visibly angry Bucaram said that a country with a crime rate as high as the United States was in no position to criticise Ecuador.
"In other places you have cocaine, in other places you have prostitution, in other places you have violence and crime. You don't see that here," he said.
U.S. ambassador Leslie Alexander warned on Wednesday that increasing corruption could put future investment by U.S. firms at risk.
"The most serious thing is that corruption is growing and becoming systematic," he told businessmen, "I'm sorry to say this, but Ecuador is winning a reputation of being riddled with corruption."
